complaint.name: Synthetic Customer 038
complaint.title: [DEMO C038] Sheets works in Platform but appears disconnected in MCP
complaint.description: The customer connected Google Sheets in the Platform, but the MCP client still requests authentication and cannot execute spreadsheet jobs.

hypotheses.description: Most likely cause: Cedar's failed Google Sheets executions on MCP required an MCP-scoped Sheets connection, but only a Platform-surface connection was active. The observed request failed on connect_mcp with zero MCP connections available even though the Platform connection was active, and the controlled synthetic comparison reproduced failure in that state and success once a connect_mcp connection existed.
assumptions: The failing production request fields accurately reflect the connection lookup state for req-38.
The synthetic controlled comparison is representative of the observed production mechanism but does not prove every failed request in the window had the identical subtype.

hypotheses.description: Secondary explanation: MCP may have been targeting a different or absent connected account identity than the one visible in Platform, so the customer experienced this as 'connected in Platform, disconnected in MCP.' This fits the missing MCP connection state but is not directly proven because no canonical account-id or connection-id selection records were supplied.
assumptions: MCP and Platform may maintain separate connected-account inventories or explicit selection context.
No canonical identity mapping records were supplied to separate absent MCP connection from wrong MCP account selection.

hypotheses.description: Lower-confidence alternative: a shared auth/grant problem such as missing grant, revoked consent, or refresh failure. Current evidence does not support this as the leading cause because the observed failure appears to occur before provider execution and another tenant succeeded against the same provider in the same window.
assumptions: If a shared Sheets credential path were failing broadly, additional canonical grant/refresh or provider-egress errors would likely be present.
An active Platform connection flag alone does not fully prove grant health for all uses, only that shared-auth failure is less consistent with this observed pre-provider 401.

recommended_actions: Synthetic telemetry supports treating this as connection_surface_isolation first: have the customer authenticate Google Sheets through the MCP flow used by this client rather than assuming the existing Platform connection is shared.

Collect missing canonical production telemetry for failing req-38-class requests: MCP connection lookup/selection, workspace/project mapping, and any auth-service grant/refresh lineage, to distinguish surface isolation from wrong connected account or project/context mismatch. These actions are proposed only and have not been executed.
If multiple Sheets identities are possible, verify the MCP workflow is bound to the intended connected account and not only to the Platform-visible account.
Continue to monitor tenant-scoped impact for Cedar versus unaffected tenants; observed impact was substantial in Cedar and not service-wide.
Do not attribute this incident to provider outage or broad tool-executor regression based on the supplied evidence alone.
limitations: The reproduce records are synthetic controlled observations, useful for discrimination but not independent proof of all production failures.

No canonical MCP connection lookup internals, account-id selection logs, or project/workspace boundary records were supplied, so wrong_connected_account and project-boundary subtypes cannot be fully separated.
No canonical auth-service grant/refresh or provider-egress attempt records were supplied for the failing execution, so shared credential failure remains an unverified alternative.
Empty deployment/dependency search results cannot prove absence of all relevant changes; they only limit what was observed in supplied telemetry.

findings.statement: The canonical Cedar failure was a 401 on request_surface=connect_mcp while connection_surface=platform, with zero MCP connections available even though a Platform connection was active.

In synthetic controlled comparison, the same request failed when MCP had zero connections and only the Platform connection was active, but succeeded when a connect_mcp connection existed while the Platform connection still remained active.

The observed failure is more consistent with connection availability or selection before provider execution than with a provider outage: provider API reachability was generally true, and another tenant had a same-window successful same-provider read.

Observed impact was substantial but tenant-scoped: Cedar had 585 requests with 375 failures, 375 business operations blocked, queue depth 105, and p95 latency 1400 ms, while Maple had 505 requests with 0 failures, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.
Observed impact was tenant-isolated rather than service-wide: Maple remained healthy and completed an unrelated successful read against the same provider during the same window.

The failed MCP request resolved against a Platform-surface connection state, which is consistent with MCP targeting a different or absent connected account/context than the one the customer sees in Platform.

The supplied evidence does not include canonical MCP connection lookup internals, account-id selection records, workspace/project boundary records, or auth grant/refresh lineage for the failing execution, so surface isolation versus account/context subtype cannot be fully separated from telemetry alone.
The only observed deployment record in the supplied evidence was an unrelated support-dashboard release, which does not support attributing the incident to a contemporaneous tool-executor rollout.

tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.

Using null filters first, what canonical records show the MCP-side authentication prompt and the failed Sheets job attempts for incident window 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z to 2026-11-12T10:15:00Z, and do those records indicate whether execution stopped before provider call, during connection lookup, or at token/grant refresh? Also compare affected-tenant failure count/latency with any unaffected tenant or other tool executions in the same service window to determine scope and whether this is isolated versus service-wide.

What exact connection model is in use between Platform and MCP for Google Sheets in this period: are they expected to share credentials, or are they separate auth surfaces? Check for recent changes around tool-executor auth lookup, connection resolution, account selection, project/workspace boundaries, or MCP-specific connection handling near the incident start, but treat timing only as hypothesis until tied to observed records.

Among the leading mechanisms—connection_surface_isolation, wrong_connected_account/account_selection_mismatch, missing_grant or revoked consent/refresh failure, project_boundary_mismatch, and internal tool-executor regression—what discriminating evidence exists for each? Specifically, can we show whether the customer’s Platform connection is valid in its own surface while MCP references a different or absent connection identity, versus a shared backend credential failing consistently across both surfaces?
Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
Write the evidence-backed internal report and proposed next steps.

objections: The top-level version/deployment finding is slightly overstated: ev_a392479ede3a/sheets-plane-038:deployments:0 only proves an unrelated support-dashboard release occurred, not by itself that no tool-executor deployment happened. The separate no-record deployment query cannot be cited as a finding record, so that claim should stay weaker and scoped as a telemetry limitation rather than proof.

notes: Canonical MCP-side auth prompt/failure record in the incident window is tool-executor log req-38 for tenant cedar at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z: status 401 on googlesheets from request_surface=connect_mcp, with connection_surface=platform, connect_mcp_connection_count=0, and platform_connection_active=true; this shows MCP did not see its own usable connection even though a Platform connection was active. Citation: ev_aefad6f5dea8 / sheets-plane-038:logs:0.

These canonical records indicate a pre-provider failure at connection availability/selection time rather than a provider call or token/grant refresh: the failed request is an MCP connect/auth surface 401 with zero MCP connections while provider reachability is generally true for the service dependency. I do not see canonical token refresh/grant error records or provider egress attempt records for the failed Sheets execution in the supplied evidence, so refresh-specific attribution remains unverified. Citations: ev_aefad6f5dea8 / sheets-plane-038:logs:0; ev_3b897096197e / sheets-plane-038:dependencies:0.

Scope appears tenant-isolated rather than service-wide in the observed window. Cedar shows 585 requests, 375 failures, 375 business operations blocked, queue_depth 105, p95 latency 1400 ms, while comparison tenant maple shows 505 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms; maple also has a 200 successful unrelated read at the same timestamp. Citations: ev_afb0d9c7104d / sheets-plane-038:metrics:0; ev_afb0d9c7104d / sheets-plane-038:metrics:1; ev_67af2dd10c48 / sheets-plane-038:logs:1.

A controlled sandbox comparison is consistent with surface isolation: with the original setup, connect_mcp_connection_count=0 plus platform_connection_active=true produced 401, while a corrected condition using a connect_mcp connection count of 1 produced 200. This supports the observed mechanism but is not independent proof of production cause. Citations: ev_45fee10ce9dc / sheets-plane-038:reproduce:0; ev_45fee10ce9dc / sheets-plane-038:reproduce:1.

Observed execution uses distinct surfaces rather than shared credentials: the failed Cedar request came from request_surface=connect_mcp while resolving against connection_surface=platform, with platform_connection_active=true but connect_mcp_connection_count=0, and it returned 401; in the controlled sandbox, the same request failed in that state and passed only when a connect_mcp connection existed, even while the Platform connection remained active (ev_aefad6f5dea8/sheets-plane-038:logs:0; ev_45fee10ce9dc/sheets-plane-038:reproduce:0; ev_45fee10ce9dc/sheets-plane-038:reproduce:1).

This supports a likely connection-surface isolation model for Google Sheets during the incident window: a Platform Sheets connection alone was not sufficient for MCP execution, and MCP appears to expect its own connection/account on the connect_mcp surface for these observed requests (ev_45fee10ce9dc/sheets-plane-038:reproduce:0; ev_45fee10ce9dc/sheets-plane-038:reproduce:1; ev_aefad6f5dea8/sheets-plane-038:logs:0).

Impact was tenant-specific, not service-wide: Cedar saw 375/585 failures (~64%), 375 business operations blocked, queue depth 105, p95 latency 1400 ms, while Maple had 0/505 failures, no backlog, and p95 160 ms; Maple also had an unrelated successful read, which argues against a provider-wide Google Sheets outage or broad tool-executor auth failure (ev_afb0d9c7104d/sheets-plane-038:metrics:0; ev_afb0d9c7104d/sheets-plane-038:metrics:1; ev_67af2dd10c48/sheets-plane-038:logs:1).

No canonical evidence here shows a recent tool-executor auth/connection deployment or explicit MCP lookup/account-selection code change near start time: broad and auth-targeted tool-executor deployment queries returned no records, and dependency search results did not expose MCP/connection-specific internals. That is a telemetry gap, so timing-based change hypotheses remain unverified (ev_0f8f87bf4c6d has no records; ev_e4c85dd3f365 has no records; ev_ecc05a57894e has no records; ev_d5def1711d53 has no records).

payload.question: Among the leading mechanisms—connection_surface_isolation, wrong_connected_account/account_selection_mismatch, missing_grant or revoked consent/refresh failure, project_boundary_mismatch, and internal tool-executor regression—what discriminating evidence exists for each? notes: Strongest discriminating evidence favors Platform-valid but MCP-absent connection state, not a shared backend credential failing across both surfaces.
